log.action: Shout a challenge to the armed men nearby.
log.narration: Turn 1 | Day 1, 6:02 pmYour voice cracks out over the wind like a whip of its own."Steel's drawn! Show yourselves or fight in the open like men, not jackals in the ash!"The nearest wagon lurches to a halt, its team screaming, and a lean shape drops from the driver's board with a saber already gleaming dull in the fading light. Two more spill from behind the second wagon, leather and mail creaking, and one of them barks a laugh that has no mirth in it at all. Then a fourth voice rises above the rest, unhurried, almost pleased, and the ash-fog parts enough to show you a face carved from old memory: scarred jaw, iron rings through the ear, a grin you have seen across a pit floor slick with blood."Well now. Iron Wolf himself, standing in the road like he's waiting for us."🔊………

log.action: Duck into the ash-fog to scout unseen.
log.narration: Turn 2 | Day 1, 6:02 pmStealth checkd20: 13 -- successYou drop low and let the drifting ash swallow you whole, boots silent on packed earth, breath held tight against your teeth. The fog curls around your shoulders like a living thing, and through its grey veil you count them proper now: Theron at the center, unhurried, savoring this, and the two thugs fanning wide to flank where you stood a heartbeat ago. Behind them the wagons groan, chained shapes shifting in the dark beds, captives you cannot yet see but can surely hear, a low frightened murmur under the wind. Theron's grin doesn't waver. He knows this game too well to be rattled by a man vanishing into smoke."Skulking now? That's not the Korrag I remember. Come out and take your welcome like a wolf, not a rat."🔊………

log.action: Shout a challenge to the armed men nearby.
log.narration: Turn 3 | Day 1, 6:03 pmYou could stay hidden and strike from the smoke, but that isn't your way, never has been. You straighten out of the ash-fog and let them see you plain, longsword catching the last dirty light of dusk."I'm no rat, Theron. Call your dogs off those wagons or I'll put you in the ground where you belong."Theron laughs, low and delighted, and spreads his hands like a man greeting an old friend at a tavern door."Dogs? These are my brothers, Korrag. Come stand with us again. Coin, and no master over you but me. Or die here in the ash for people who'd never spit on your grave."The two thugs shift closer, blades low, waiting on his word, and somewhere behind the wagons a woman sobs once and goes silent, as if she knows better than to hope.🔊………

log.action: Charge Theron Wyndfall while he gloats.
log.narration: Turn 4 | Day 1, 6:04 pmStrength attack rolld20: 18 -- hitYou don't answer him with words. You answer with your feet, closing the ground between you in three long strides, ash kicking up in your wake like smoke off a grass fire. Theron's grin falters half a heartbeat too late, his saber coming up in a clumsy guard as you declare your strength and put your whole body behind the blade.Steel meets flesh where his collarbone meets his neck, and he staggers back with a snarl, blood already darkening his jerkin.Theron catches his balance against the wagon wheel, spitting a curse through gritted teeth, and the two thugs break from their flanking positions to close on you from either side, blades rising.🔊………

log.action: Refuse Theron and attack him head-on.
log.narration: Turn 5 | Day 1, 6:05 pmStrength attack rolld20: 15 -- hitDexterity attack roll (Slaver Thug)d20: 11 -- missTheron's already reeling, one hand pressed to the wound at his collarbone, but he's a pit-fighter same as you once were, and he doesn't go down easy. You drive in again before he can set his feet, longsword whistling in a short brutal arc.The blade bites deep across his ribs and he howls, stumbling sideways into the wagon's traces, the horses screaming and jerking against their harness."You'll bleed for this, Iron Wolf! Kill him! KILL HIM!"The nearest thug lunges in at your exposed flank, short blade flashing low toward your ribs while his fellow circles wide for your back.Steel scrapes off your chainmail with a sound like a struck bell, and the thug curses, off balance from the wasted swing.🔊………

log.action: Turn and strike the nearest flanking thug.
log.narration: Turn 6 | Day 1, 6:06 pmStrength attack rolld20: 16 -- hitYou pivot on your back foot, letting Theron stagger where he stands, and put your shoulder into the thug still recovering from his wasted lunge. Your blade comes around low to high, the same motion that's put a hundred pit-dogs in the dirt.The longsword opens him from hip to ribs and he folds with a wet grunt, sliding off your blade to crumple in the ash, his weapon falling from nerveless fingers.One thug down and cooling in the road. Theron staggers upright against the wagon wheel, blood soaking his jerkin black in the dying light, and the second thug hangs back now, eyes flicking between you and his bleeding captain, courage draining fast. Behind the wagons the captives' murmur has turned to something sharper, hope maybe, or terror that the wrong side might win."Get up, you gutless whoreson, HELP ME!"🔊………

log.action: Finish off wounded Theron with a killing blow.
log.narration: Turn 7 | Day 1, 6:07 pmStrength attack rolld20: 20 -- critical hitTheron sees it coming and tries to raise his saber, but his arm's gone weak with blood loss, and the guard comes up too slow, too late. You drive your longsword forward with everything the north ever taught you, straight through the gap his stagger left open.The blade takes him under the ribs and up, and Theron Wyndfall makes a sound like a man surprised by his own death, which he is. He slides off the steel and down into the ash, eyes already fixed on nothing, and the road goes quiet save for the wind and the horses stamping in their traces.The last thug doesn't wait to see if you're finished. He drops his blade in the ash and bolts north into the dark, boots pounding, and doesn't look back once. Behind the wagons, chains rattle, and a voice, cracked and disbelieving, calls out from the shadows between the wheels."Gods above... he's actually killed him. Killed Wyndfall."🔊………

log.action: Shout at the captives to stay back.
log.narration: Turn 8 | Day 1, 6:07 pmYou wheel toward the wagons, blade still red, and bark out over the wind before anyone does something stupid."Stay in the wagons! Fighting's done, but I don't know you from the ash yet, so stay back till I say otherwise!"The murmuring behind the slatted wood goes still, chains clinking as bodies press away from the sound of your voice. Orvun's the only one who answers, dragging himself up against the wheel to get a better look at you."They're saying down the South Road that some outlander wolf turned on his own pack tonight, refused Wyndfall's offer clean to his face and gutted him for the insult. Didn't believe it till now."🔊………

log.action: Go to the captives chained behind the wagons.
log.narration: Turn 9 | Day 1, 6:07 pmYou sheathe your blade, wiping what you can of the blood on your thigh, and step past Theron's cooling body toward the wagons. The wood groans as you round the tailgate, and there they are, six or seven souls crouched in the straw and their own filth, wrists and ankles bound in iron, eyes catching what little dusk light remains like animals cornered too long to trust rescue when it comes.Orvun drags himself upright against the wheel, chains rattling, and studies you with the wary hope of a man who's seen kindness turn to cruelty before."You mean to free us, or just pick over what Wyndfall left behind? I'll not blame you either way, only tell me straight."🔊………

log.action: Check the wagons for more captives.
log.narration: Turn 10 | Day 1, 6:07 pmWisdom check (searching wagons)d20: 13 -- successYou move down the line of wagons, boots crunching ash and gravel, checking each bed in turn. Most sit near empty, straw and old chains and nothing else, whoever they held either sold off already or never loaded at all. The last wagon holds the rest of them, huddled together against the slats, gaunt faces turning up at you with the same wary flicker Orvun wore a moment before.You count six souls total chained in that last bed, Orvun among them, no others hidden beneath false floors or false hope. Whatever Wyndfall meant to do with this lot, market or worse, it ends here in the ash with him."Six of us left. There were more, three days back, sold off at some crossing east of here before I lost count of the days."🔊………

log.action: Ask Orvun about the other captives.
log.narration: Turn 11 | Day 1, 6:17 pmYou crouch by the tailgate, close enough that Orvun doesn't have to shout over the wind."The ones sold off. Where were they taken, and who bought them?"Orvun's chains rattle as he shifts, and something bitter crosses his face, the look of a man forced to remember names he'd rather forget."A trader met Wyndfall's wagons at a river crossing, paid in coin I never saw the count of. Northlanders mostly, strong backs, the kind that fetch a price in Ashenveil's pits. Wyndfall bragged the buyer serves some lord in the city who pays double for fighters who don't die easy. Never got a name past that. Wyndfall wasn't one to share his masters' business with cargo."🔊………

log.action: Break the captives' chains free.
log.narration: Turn 12 | Day 1, 6:32 pmYou take up the iron ring bolted to the wagon floor and set your boot against the boards for leverage. The chain is old, half rusted through by ash and rain, and it gives way under a single wrench of your shoulders. One by one you work down the line, snapping links or twisting pins loose, and one by one the captives sit up straighter, rubbing raw wrists like men waking from a fever.Orvun is the last, and he watches his own chain fall to the boards like he doesn't quite believe the sound of it."Free men again. Small thing to you, maybe. Not to us."The others say nothing yet, just breathe, some of them weeping without sound, one big Northlander flexing scarred hands like he's testing whether they still remember how to make a fist.🔊………

log.action: Ask Orvun about Ashenveil's fighting pits.
log.narration: Turn 13 | Day 1, 6:42 pmYou settle back on your heels, studying Orvun's face in the dying light, ash still sifting down between you like grey rain that never quite stops."Tell me what you know of these pits. Who runs them, and what a man walks into if he's dragged there in chains."Orvun rubs at his wrists, working feeling back into hands that have forgotten freedom, and his eyes go distant, remembering things he'd rather not."I never saw the inside, only heard the traders talk when they thought captives couldn't understand plain speech. There's an arena somewhere in the low quarter, walled off from decent eyes, run for some lord's amusement and some lord's coin. Fighters go in chained and don't always come out the same men. Talk was some of them get stronger than flesh has right to be, faster, meaner, like something's been poured into them that isn't blood. Wyndfall called it a blessing when he was selling the idea to buyers. I call it a curse dressed up in gold."The wind shifts, carrying the reek of the Blighted Reach fresh off the eastern trail, and Orvun's gaze flicks that direction like the thought unsettles him more than the pits themselves."Whatever's done to them, I'd wager it comes from out there. Nothing good ever came riding west on that wind."🔊………

log.action: Search Theron's body for coin or clues.
log.narration: Turn 14 | Day 1, 6:42 pmInvestigation checkd20: 16 -- successYou leave the wagons behind and cross to where Theron Wyndfall lies cooling in the ash, the ground beneath him gone black and stiff with old blood. You crouch and go through his jerkin with the brisk, unsentimental hands of a man who has looted corpses before and felt nothing much doing it.A leather purse yields a handful of coin, not a fortune but enough to matter. Tucked inside his boot you find a scrap of oilcloth wrapped around a folded paper, a bill of sale scrawled in a clerk's cramped hand, naming no lord outright but marked with a wax seal pressed in the shape of a crowned skull, and beneath it a single line of instruction: deliver to the warehouse on Cinder Row, ask for Zethran, speak the words "the King is bound" at the gate.You turn the seal over in your fingers, the crowned skull catching the last grey light, and something cold moves through your gut that has nothing to do with the wind. Whatever waits on Cinder Row, it isn't ordinary slaving business. It smells of something older and worse, the kind of thing your Northland blood was raised to distrust on sight.🔊………

log.action: Search the wagons for anything useful to the captives.
log.narration: Turn 15 | Day 1, 6:42 pmYou leave Theron where he lies and pick back through the wagons, kicking through straw and old sacking for anything worth the taking. The empty beds give up little, a coil of spare rope, a waterskin gone half dry, a rusted lantern with no oil left to burn. In the driver's box of the lead wagon you find a strongbox, unlocked and half-forgotten, holding a few tools and a stack of rough wool blankets meant for cold nights on the road.You toss the blankets back to the captives first, since the wind cuts colder now that dusk is falling proper, and Orvun catches one and wraps it round a woman beside him who hasn't stopped shivering since her chains came off."Small mercies. We'll take them."The road south lies open toward Ashenveil's gate, the wagon trail waits east into the Blighted Reach, and six freed souls are looking to you now for what comes next.🔊………

log.action: Do something reckless.
log.narration: Turn 16 | Day 1, 7:42 pmWisdom check (reckless pursuit through failing light)d20: 19 -- successYou've had enough of half-plans and careful counting. You stride to the lead wagon, seize the harness of the draft horses, and instead of leading them south at a walk toward the safety of the gate, you swing up onto the driver's board and haul the reins hard east, straight down the wagon trail toward the Blighted Reach itself, toward the river crossing Orvun named, where the rest of the sold Northlanders passed three days gone. If there's a chance of catching that trader before he vanishes into Ashenveil's underworld, it lies that way, and you mean to run the horses to lathering exhaustion to find it.The wagon lurches and rattles over root and stone, ash swirling up behind the wheels like the ghost of the road itself, and the captives cling to the slats white-knuckled as you drive on past dusk and into the dark. But the gamble pays. Barely two miles on, where the trail dips through a gully choked with dead brush, your torchlight catches wagon ruts freshly cut, and beyond them the dying embers of a cookfire, still faintly warm. A second party passed through here, recent, moving slow, burdened. The trader's trail is not cold. It is hours old, not days.🔊………

log.action: I accept the offer: The Trader's Trail.
log.narration: Turn 17 | Day 1, 7:47 pmYou rein the horses to a snorting halt at the gully's edge, ash sifting into the ruts like the land itself was trying to bury the evidence. The choice settles into your gut, cold and certain as a blade going home. You will run this trader down before Ashenveil swallows him and the last of his captives both."Trail's warm. We ride till it's cold or he's dead."Orvun says nothing, only grips the wagon rail tighter, and behind him the freed Northlanders go quiet, listening to the wind carry the smell of another fire somewhere ahead in the dark.🔊………

log.action: Ask Orvun what he knows of this trail.
log.narration: Turn 18 | Day 1, 7:57 pmYou drop the reins loose in your fist and half-turn on the driver's board, ash catching in your beard like grey frost. Orvun climbs up beside you, careful of his healing wrists, and squints east where the torchlight dies against the dark."You said Wyndfall sold others before us. This the same road they took?""Same road, aye. He'd send the strong ones ahead in smaller lots, easier to move quiet that way. Less chains rattling, fewer eyes counting heads at the crossing." He nods toward the gully, toward the dead fire. "That crossing's another hour on, maybe less if the ground holds. River's shallow there, fordable, but the far bank's thick with bramble. A wagon'd have to slow to a crawl getting through it."His eyes flick to you, wary still, but something else creeping in behind the caution."You mean to catch him before the bramble. Don't you."🔊………

log.action: Tell Orvun to keep the captives quiet.
log.narration: Turn 19 | Day 1, 8:07 pmYou twist back toward the wagon bed, voice pitched low and hard, the kind of tone that carries without shouting."Keep them quiet back there. No crying, no chains rattling. Sound carries further than fire out here."Orvun nods once and drops back among the huddled Northlanders, murmuring something low that stills the worst of the shivering and the whispered prayers. The wagon creaks on into the dark, ash hissing faint against the wheels, and but for the horses' breath and the wind combing through dead brush, the night swallows you whole and silent.🔊………

log.action: Skip ahead — a montage to the next real decision.
log.narration: Turn 20 | Day 1, 11:07 pmThe wagon grinds on through hours of dark, the horses lathered and blowing hard, and you keep the pace just short of ruinous, reading the ruts by torchlight where the ground turns soft and the trail threatens to vanish into scrub.  Twice you lose the trail where stone breaks up the dirt, and twice you find it again, casting wide on foot with the torch low until the wheel-marks resume east of a fallen deadwood. The freed Northlanders doze fitfully against each other in the wagon bed, and Orvun keeps his word, hushing the ones who whimper in their sleep, while the ash thins overhead and stars claw through the smoke haze. Near the bottom of the third hour the ground begins to slope and the air turns damp and cold, the smell of running water threading up through the burnt-iron stink of the Reach, and ahead through the black trees you catch the flat gleam of a river and, faint but unmistakable, torchlight moving slow along its far bank.🔊………

log.action: Push the horses toward the river crossing.
log.narration: Turn 21 | Day 1, 11:17 pmStrength check (driving the team down a rough slope)d20: 16 -- successYou crack the reins hard and the horses lunge down the slope, hooves skidding in loose scree, the wagon rocking so violently the chains still bolted to the floorboards clatter like dying bells. Branches lash the sides as you crash through the last stand of trees, and the river opens up before you, black water running fast and cold under the stars, torches bobbing on the far bank where the trader's party works its slow way through the bramble.The wagon hits the shallows in a spray of freezing water, the horses screaming protest, but you hold the line true and drive them straight across, the ford barely deep enough to wet the axles. Ahead on the far bank a shout goes up, distant but sharp with alarm, and torches swing round toward the sound of your crossing. You've found them. Whether they've found trouble or a fight, that's still yours to decide.🔊………

log.action: Skip ahead — a montage to the next real decision.
log.narration: Turn 22 | Day 1, 11:37 pmBut the shout on the far bank dies as quickly as it rose, no answering charge, no rush of steel, only distant torches drawing together into a knot and then, strangely, holding still. You keep the wagon moving along the bank at a walk, letting the horses blow, Orvun crouched at the rail with his eyes fixed on that unmoving cluster of light.  The wind shifts and carries voices across the water, low and arguing, not the panic of men caught but the sour tone of men bargaining, and beneath it you catch the creak of wagon wheels that have stopped rolling. A quarter hour on, the trees break and you see it plain: the trader's party has halted at a second crossing further downstream, wagons drawn into a rough circle, torches ringing something or someone at their center.🔊………

log.action: Shout a challenge across the water.
log.narration: Turn 23 | Day 1, 11:37 pmYou stand tall in the wagon box and let your voice roll out over the black water like thunder rolling down a mountainside."Trader! I know what you carry and I know what you are! Stand and answer for it, or run and die tired!"The torches at the far ring freeze, then scatter into motion, men shouting to each other in a scramble you can't yet read as fight or flight. Beside you Orvun grips the rail, his knuckles pale, and mutters low."They're already talking about you south of here. Some say you butchered Wyndfall for his coin, not his cruelty. Others say you're carving your way through every slaver in the Reach to free your own people. Ash-cursed fools don't know which lie to spread faster."Whatever the trader decides in the next few heartbeats, it will not be quiet.🔊………

log.action: Drive the wagon straight into their firelight.
log.narration: Turn 24 | Day 1, 11:37 pmDexterity check (controlling the team through rough, firelit ground)d20: 13 -- successYou haul the reins hard and lash the horses forward, no more caution left in you, driving the team straight down the bank and into the ring of torchlight before the trader's men can decide whether to run.The wagon crashes through their loose picket line, scattering a fire-lit knot of men who dive clear of the wheels, and you haul the horses up hard in the center of their camp, dust and ash boiling up around you in the torchlight. Wagons ring you close, and a lean man in a slaver's leather coat spins to face you with a hand already dropping to a curved knife at his hip, flanked by two rough hired swords who spread wide with weapons rising."You. The northland dog from the crossroads. Sweet mother of ruin, you followed us."His eyes flick to your longsword, then to the chained shapes huddled behind his own wagons, weighing whether to fight or flee in the space of a breath.🔊………

log.action: Watch to see if they flee or fight.
log.narration: Turn 25 | Day 1, 11:37 pmYou hold the reins taut, blade already loose in its sheath, and give the trader half a heartbeat to choose his own ending."Kill him! Kill him now, before he does what he did to Wyndfall!"His voice cracks with more fear than command, and the two guards flanking him hesitate, trading a look that says they've heard exactly how that story ends. One steps forward anyway, sword raised, jaw set hard. The other's feet shift backward half a pace, torchlight catching the sweat on his brow, morale already cracking before steel ever meets steel.🔊………

log.action: Attack the two hired swords first.
log.narration: Turn 26 | Day 1, 11:37 pmAttack roll (Strength, longsword)d20: 17 -- hitDamage roll (longsword + Power Strike)d20: 11 -- significant woundYou leave the trader shouting behind his wagon and drive straight at the nearer guard, the one who stepped forward, longsword sweeping up into a vicious arc aimed at his ribs.Power Strike blazes through the blow, steel biting deep through leather and meat before the man can even finish his guard.He folds sideways with a strangled cry, clutching a wound that's already soaking his tunic black, and staggers hard into the wagon wheel behind him. The second guard, the wavering one, goes white at the sight of it, his blade drooping half an inch as if the weight of the fight just doubled in his hands.🔊………

log.action: Demand the trader release the captives now.
log.narration: Turn 27 | Day 1, 11:37 pmYou wheel your horse half around, bloody blade still raised, and bellow past the guards straight at the trader cowering behind his own wagon."Loose the chains now and you walk out of this with your throat whole! Test me again and you die where Wyndfall died!""You're mad, you're mad, I paid good coin for that stock, I've a buyer waiting in the city, you'll ruin me!"His voice pitches high with panic, more merchant than fighter, and he clutches his little curved knife like it might somehow hold back a storm. The wounded guard sags further against the wheel, done for the fight in all but name, while the second guard's blade drops another inch, eyes darting toward the tree line as if measuring the distance to somewhere else entirely.🔊………

log.action: Press the attack on the wavering guard.
log.narration: Turn 28 | Day 1, 11:37 pmAttack roll (Strength, longsword)d20: 14 -- hitDamage roll (longsword)d20: 6 -- solid woundYou pivot hard off the horse's flank and drive at the second guard before his nerve finishes breaking, longsword hissing down in a short, brutal cut.The blade opens his forearm to the bone and the sword spins loose from his grip, clattering into the ash. He doesn't even reach for it. He throws both hands up, stumbling backward into the firelight, blood sheeting down to his elbow."Mercy! Mercy, I yield, I yield, don't gut me like the captain!"The trader's eyes go wide with betrayal at his own man's collapse, and he backs another step toward the wagons, knife shaking in his fist, alone now but for a man still bleeding out against a wheel.🔊………

log.action: Shout for the wavering guard to surrender.
log.narration: Turn 29 | Day 1, 11:37 pmThe guard's already on his knees with his hands thrown skyward, blood running warm down to his fingers, so your shout only drives the point home harder."Down, then, and stay down! Move again and it'll be the last thing you do!""Down! I'm down! Gods, I'm down, just don't, don't-"He presses his forehead near to the ash, shivering, and goes still as a man playing dead can manage. The trader stands alone now in the wreck of his own camp, torches guttering around him, his eyes flicking between your bloody sword and the wagon full of chained Northlanders behind him like a man doing arithmetic he already knows he's lost.🔊………

log.action: Do something reckless.
log.narration: Turn 30 | Day 1, 11:37 pmStrength check (grapple)d20: 19 -- successYou throw down your sword arm and vault clean off the horse's back, boots slamming into the ash not three strides from the trader's knife, and instead of finishing him you seize the man by the throat with your bare hand and haul him bodily into the firelight for every captive in the wagon to see.He claws uselessly at your wrist, feet kicking air, knife falling forgotten into the dirt. You don't kill him. You wrench him around to face the wagon full of chained Northlanders and roar past his ear."Look at them! Look at what you sell! You want to live, you give me every key on your belt, right now, and you ride out of the Reach with nothing but your skin!""Keys, yes, yes, they're, they're on my belt, take them, gods, take them all!"His hands shake so hard the iron ring rattles as he fumbles it free, and he drops it into your palm like it burns him. Behind the wagon slats, low disbelieving murmurs rise from the captives, chains shifting as they crane to see the wolf who has just brought their captor to his knees without spending a drop more blood.🔊………

log.action: Free the chained captives from the wagon.
log.narration: Turn 31 | Day 1, 11:37 pmThe trader's yielded his keys and his nerve both, choked half-senseless in your grip, and you let him drop gasping to the ash rather than spend more steel on a beaten man.You leave him wheezing in the dirt and cross to the wagon, keys jangling in your fist, and the locks give way one by one under your hands. The chains fall in the ash like dead snakes, and the captives spill out slow and disbelieving, rubbing raw wrists, staring at you like a man who's walked out of a story they didn't believe in."Wyndfall's dead, and now this one too? Who are you, that slavers fall before you like wheat?"One of them, a broad-shouldered woman with a Northland brand scarred half-healed on her forearm, steps forward and studies your face hard in the firelight, like she's hunting for something she recognizes.🔊………

log.action: Unlock the wagon with the keys.
log.narration: Turn 32 | Day 1, 11:37 pmThe last lock gives with a heavy clunk, and the rearmost wagon's chains slither loose into the dirt. The broad-shouldered woman with the half-healed brand steadies herself against the wagon's frame, still studying you, and speaks low enough that only you and the firelight hear it."I served under a man called Nolan Grimtide, before Wyndfall bought my chain off him. If you're hunting the ones who run this trade, that name goes higher than some road-captain with a knife."The other captives murmur at the name, and one spits into the ash like it tastes foul in his mouth. The trader, still slumped where you dropped him, flinches at the sound of it too, eyes darting up at you as though he'd hoped that name would never reach your ears.🔊………

log.action: Search the trader's belt and pockets.
log.narration: Turn 33 | Day 1, 11:37 pmInvestigation checkd20: 16 -- successYou crouch over the trader where he still huddles in the ash, and go through his belt and pockets with the same rough, practiced hands you used on Wyndfall's corpse.A small leather ledger comes free from an inner pocket, its pages cramped with names, prices, and dates in a nervous scrawl. Threaded through with those entries, one name recurs more than any other, a buyer in Ashenveil who pays premium coin for "durable stock," signed simply as Zethran. Beneath that, scrawled almost as an afterthought, another notation catches your eye, a payment routed through a woman named Morwen Ulvane, described only as "the broker who never haggles."The trader watches you read it, his face gone the color of old ash."That book's worth more than my life to the wrong people. You'd do well to burn it, not carry it."🔊………

log.action: Ask the woman about Nolan Grimtide.
log.narration: Turn 34 | Day 1, 11:37 pmYou turn from the trader and face the woman who spoke the name, the brand on her shoulder still raw and shining in the firelight. She straightens under your gaze, the fear in her easing just slightly now that the chains are gone."Grimtide. Tell me what you know of him.""He never dirtied his own hands, not that I saw. Wyndfall answered to him same as I answered to Wyndfall. Grimtide moves through market towns buying up strong backs cheap, then sells them on for triple in Ashenveil. I heard his men speak of him only in whispers, like saying his name too loud might summon him."She glances past you toward the dark road east, toward the city waiting beyond the ash and wind."If you mean to follow this thread to its end, Grimtide is the knot above Wyndfall's. But there's another name that frightens even him, or so I heard once, drunk talk from a guard who thought I was too broken to listen. A priest. Valerius."The trader, still huddled in the dirt, flinches hard at that name, and says nothing at all.🔊………

log.action: Head back toward The Crossroads of Ashenveil.
log.narration: Turn 35 | Day 1, 2:37 amYou leave the wagons and the huddled captives behind you, ash crunching underfoot as you strike back west along the trail your own reckless drive carved hours before. The freed Northlanders watch you go in silence, some already gathering blankets and rope for the walk to wherever safety might still exist in this blighted country. Dawn is still far off, and the wind keeps carrying that stink of burnt copper down from the Reach at your back.The three roads open before you again, South Road toward Ashenveil's gate, North Road into wolf country, and the wagon trail behind you now soaked in blood and old fear. Two slaver corpses still mark the crossing where Theron Wyndfall fell, stiffening in the cold, ash beginning to soften the shapes of them the way it softens everything in this dead country.
